items.title: Pre-fight controls crushed by CTA
items.what: In the pre-fight screen (screenshot 2), the massive golden 'FIGHT' button occupies the lower-middle third of the screen, pushing the dual joysticks ('STANCE' and 'TECHNIQUE') to the extreme bottom edge, leaving less than 40px of clearance.
items.why: On a 390x844 display, the bottom bezel/home-indicator area is physically difficult to reach with thumbs. Squashing the primary input controls here forces awkward hand positioning and increases missed inputs before the game even starts.
items.how: Reduce the height of the 'FIGHT' button by 25% and shift its position upward. Ensure the joysticks maintain at least 60px of padding from the bottom screen edge to accommodate the device's gesture bar and comfortable thumb reach.

items.title: Combat control hints blocking footwork
items.what: During active bouts (screenshots 3, 4, 5), the semi-transparent control hint bar ('STANCE: step, jump...' / 'TECHNIQUE: back, forward...') floats directly over the fighters' lower legs and feet.
items.why: In point karate, foot placement (stepping, crouching, jumping) is the primary mechanic. Obscuring the fighters' feet with a UI overlay removes critical visual feedback regarding distance and stance, making it harder for players to judge timing and positioning.
items.how: Move this hint panel to the top of the screen (below the timer/round info) or implement a 'fade-out' animation that hides the panel after 3 seconds of inactivity. Alternatively, make the panel thinner and position it strictly above the joysticks without overlapping the character models.

items.title: Low visibility for action buttons
items.what: The 'MOVES' and Settings gear buttons in the top-right corner (screenshots 3, 4, 5) are dark grey pills that blend into the warm, low-key dojo background lighting.
items.why: Low contrast reduces discoverability. Players scanning the screen during a fight may miss the ability to check their move list or pause settings, leading to accidental taps on the background or frustration trying to find the menu.
items.how: Add a semi-transparent dark backing (e.g., rgba(0,0,0,0.6)) or a subtle drop shadow behind these buttons to separate them from the background environment and increase legibility.

items.title: Unbalanced hit-feedback typography
items.what: On a successful point (screenshot 12), the text stack reads 'IPPON' (huge) -> 'HASANABI' (medium) -> 'SPINNING BACK KICK' (small). The technique name is disproportionately small compared to the announcer text.
items.why: The specific technique name is crucial educational feedback for a fighting game. Making it too small wastes a key teaching moment where the player just executed a complex move like a 'Spinning Back Kick'.
items.how: Increase the font size of the technique name ('SPINNING BACK KICK') by approximately 50% and tighten the vertical line-height between the three lines of text to create a more cohesive, impactful announcement block.

items.title: Broken stats line on victory screen
items.what: In the victory screen (screenshot 8), the text 'BOUTS WON 0 / 1 - BEST -' ends with 'BEST -', which is empty and looks like a broken placeholder rather than intentional design.
items.why: Visible placeholders erode polish. It suggests incomplete data handling or a missing feature, distracting the player from the actual result ('HASANABI WINS').
items.how: Remove the '- BEST -' suffix entirely until a streak or best-time metric is available. If the stat is irrelevant for a single-bout qualifier, hide the entire line or replace it with a 'Next Opponent' indicator.
